turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I'm here because... I just can't stop focusing on this spot on my face. There's this rough, kind of sunken-looking patch right here. Every time I look in the mirror or see a photo of myself, it's all I can see. It makes one side of me look just... old and beat-up. 

It's really getting to me, to be honest, especially because whenever I bring it up to anyone, they keep saying they barely notice anything at all. But I see it plain as day, and I just can't get it out of my head.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes an uncontrollable preoccupation with a perceived facial flaw that others report barely noticing at all.

turns.doctor_question: When people tell you they don't notice the spot, is there any part of you that considers they might be right, or are you completely certain that what you see is exactly how it looks to everyone else?
turns.patient_response:
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean... I hear them when they say they don't see it, but I just don't get how they can miss it. 

Sometimes I think maybe they're just being polite, you know? Or maybe they're just not looking that close. But... I don't know if I'm completely certain about how it looks to everyone else. I just know what I see when I look in the mirror, and it's right there. It's hard to just pretend it's not, even if they tell me I'm crazy for worrying about it.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from worrying about this spot on your face, do you notice similar intrusive thoughts or repetitive behaviors—like checking, counting, or needing things to feel 'just right'—in other areas of your life?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I don't have to count things or organize my tools a certain way or anything like that. When I'm at work, I just get the job done. It's really just this thing on my face that takes up all my attention. I don't have any of those other habits you mentioned.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms that the perceived defect on their face takes up all of their attention, demonstrating preoccupation with appearance.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly denies engaging in repetitive behaviors or compulsions such as counting, organizing tools in a specific way, or other ritualistic habits.

turns.doctor_question: If a dermatologist examined your skin closely and told you there was no visible abnormality at all, do you think you could accept that, or would you still be convinced the spot is really there no matter what they said?
turns.patient_response:
Man, I don't know. I'd like to think I'd take a doctor's word for it. But... if a skin doctor looked right at it and said there was absolutely nothing there? I'd probably just figure they meant it wasn't cancer or something that needed fixing medically. 

If they tried to tell me the skin is perfectly normal and smooth... I honestly don't think I could just buy that. I mean, I see it every morning when I shave. It'd be real hard to just turn off what my own two eyes are showing me, no matter who's saying it. So, yeah, I'd probably still be convinced it's there.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from this concern about the spot on your face, have you noticed any other unusual thoughts or beliefs lately—like feeling that people are watching you, talking about you, or that something else unusual is happening around you?
turns.patient_response: No, nothing like that. I don't think people are watching me or talking about me behind my back, unless they're staring at my face, you know? But no, no weird beliefs or feeling like strange things are going on. It's just the spot. Everything else in my life is pretty normal, to be honest.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies having persecutory ideas, feelings of being watched, or any other unusual beliefs or experiences.
